newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - U.S. data boosts Wall St, European bourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. data boosts Wall St, European bourses.

text.p: Fresh economic data showing that the powerhouse U.S. economy is steadily slowing -- implying U.S. interest rates might stay low -- boosted both record-breaking Wall Street and European stocks on Friday.
European shares had already been trading significantly firmer, boosted by a seventh consecutive record close on Wall Street overnight.

The Dow vaulted higher at the open in Friday and jumped 37 points or more than half a percent by 1545 GMT after unexpected news from the Federal Reserve that the U.S. had suffered its first decline in industrial output in seven months.

The news of a slowing economy means a U.S. rate hike is less likely which is good news for stocks. The converse should be true for the dollar, but in fact the U.S. currency showed little reaction and was up from its session lows against the mark and the yen.

In London, Europe's biggest bourse, the blue chip FTSE 100 index moved to its best levels -- 28 points or some three quarters of a percent up -- after Wall Street opened. It was boosted also by a firmer tone in both futures and government bond markets.
Two concerns, however, weighed on the market:

Analysts were pondering what would happen when Wall Street's bull run finally hit the buffers and worried about increasing signs that British interest rates may have to rise again soon following a sharp rise in UK retail prices in October.

"We're all expecting and waiting for Wall Street to consolidate and it's giving us a reason to hold off buying." said one head of equity sales. "We would like to see just how well our market can tolerate a U.S. consolidation."
On British rate prospects, Panmure Gordon Strategist Ian Williams commented: "The mood the market has got itself into about interest rates, we're going to see a continuation of the jitters."

German shares ended bourse trade at another record. Dealers said even the prospect of the giant Deutsche Telekom flotation on Monday was not quite enough to generate impetus needed to penetrate the magic 2,800 point level in bourse trade.
In later computerised trade, however, the IBIS DAX index reached a fresh record of 2,802.63 points.
There was heavy trade in major German banks Deutsche, Dresdner, and Commerzbank in the light of takeover and merger rumours. The DAX-30 index ended at 2,795.80 points.
In Paris French shares nudged the day's highs after the New York open, with the main CAC-40 index up 30.19 points or 1.36 percent at 2,248.37 at 1530 GMT.

A major focus of the currency markets was the pound sterling which powered ahead to a four-year high of $1.6697 against the dollar and a 30-month high of 2.5180 against the mark. Sterling's trade-weighted index rose to a 34-month high of 92.0.

The pound's latest sharp rise began on Wednesday after the minutes of the September monetary meeting between Bank of England governor Eddie George and Clarke showed that George had urged the government to raise rates to more six percent.
However, analysts warned the pound's rise could be short-lived and the prospect of a disappointing budget and low November inflation figures could be lying in wait to ambush it.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5078 marks and 110.97 yen compared with 1.5096 marks and 111.31 yen late in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had risen 28 points to 3,954.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index gained 30.19 to 2,248.37.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 18.79 at 2,795.8.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixes at $379.25 compared with $382.50 at the London close on Thursday. Silver was easier at $4.85.
